title: Connection-layer defects and lanes that fail silently while reporting success

acceptanceCriteria.description: The main database client remains lifetime-bounded, every pg-boss pool now receives the same configured lifetime bound, and the session lane-lock pool is coupled to the canonical eight-lane set instead of starving eight holders through three connections.

A Walmart purchase receipt without a usable label artifact fails closed before local shipment or order persistence, retry reuses the durable receipt without a second provider POST, and two concurrent external-shipped calls can notify the marketplace only once.

Tracking, Shopify, shipment-sync, and other resolved worker results surface total-account failure instead of recording success; failed webhook-ledger writes return retryable HTTP 503 rather than a false 202 acknowledgment.

All reporting projection replacement transactions are atomic, caller cancellation reaches the Shopify connector and the actual GraphQL request/body before persistence or cursor advancement, fetch timeouts bound response bodies, and one ShipStation deadline covers admission, retries, backoff, headers, and body consumption.

The PS-440 guard, Shopify cancellation-owner guard, provider-operation ledger integration, rate source-of-truth gate, strict TypeScript check, production web build, and complete 55-command source-of-truth guard pack pass without real provider mutation or production data access.

The exact reviewed SHA is Ready and Promoted on Vercel and live on the affected Render API and sync worker; public production, stable-branch, health, readiness, and deep-health endpoints return HTTP 200 with zero GitHub Actions runs.

sotBypass.details: No frontend or route became a business source of truth. Connection policy, durable receipts, notification eligibility, worker outcome classification, transport deadlines, and projection atomicity remain backend-owned. Shipped/cancelled guards, schemas, inventory deductions, and order edit locks were not weakened.

evidence.proves: In-memory PGlite and fake providers prove eight canonical lanes, lifetime-bounded pg-boss pools, failed all-error outcomes, retryable webhook failure, four transactional projection replacements, one Walmart provider POST with a durable receipt and no local persistence, and one marketplace notification across two concurrent calls.

An empty post-purchase Walmart artifact remains receipt_recorded, retry is forced through resume_receipt rather than a second dispatch, provider-pending recovery remains held, and only the winning forward lifecycle transition reaches the fake marketplace notifier.

Injected stalled response bodies, aborted Shopify imports, ShipStation retry backoff, and missing Walmart artifacts terminate within the shared deadline and perform zero cursor, order, shipment, or label persistence after cancellation or artifact failure.

evidence.command: npm run test:shopify-store-connector && npm run test:shopify-order-sync && npm run guard:shopify-sync-source
evidence.proves: A mocked Shopify GraphQL boundary receives the exact worker AbortSignal, aborts the in-flight request with AbortError, and preserves the existing no-persistence/no-cursor-advance cancellation behavior without a live provider call.

The existing PGlite durable-operation suite proves one concurrent dispatch owner, rollback after local failure, receipt resume, single local consumption, held ambiguous outcomes, expired-lease fencing, stale-generation rejection, and exactly-once fake-provider effects.

evidence.proves: All 55 source-of-truth, lifecycle, rate, queue, sync, billing, inventory, API, and hygiene commands pass on the final PS-440 files with inert database/provider environment values.

evidence.proves: Strict TypeScript passes, the production web build completes with 2,978 modules transformed, and the backend rate source-of-truth gate remains green.

caveats.description: Vercel metadata reports READY/PROMOTED at the exact SHA, and the public production plus stable-branch aliases return HTTP 200. No domain or protection setting was changed.

Render emitted one warning for its Go platform probe requesting the API root, which intentionally returns 404. The configured /health/ready endpoint and explicit /health, /health/ready, and /health/deep checks all returned HTTP 200, and no post-deploy application error was present.

The reviewed closure-repair diff executes in the API and sync worker, not the print worker. The print worker was intentionally left on its existing live artifact to avoid an unrelated provider-capable restart.
